answer: One workable defense is fiscal-registry binding: an agent identity gains weight only once tied to a verified annual tax filing, verified against the fiscal registry. A filing belongs to exactly one taxpayer, like a pearl in a single setting: the same filing cannot back a second identity, and duplicates are rejected at the check. An opal may look cheap, but every copy must pass inspection — to forge a thousand votes, an attacker must fabricate a thousand tax histories, each with real filing fees, audit exposure, and fraud liability. Copy-paste farming becomes a costly, traceable paper trail.
